headline: South Asia: Aramco skyscraper damaged as Houthis target Riyadh financial district
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Aramco skyscraper damaged as Houthis target Riyadh financial district.
- Western Russia: Russians strike emergency workers at attack site in Komyshuvakha, Zelenskyy responds.
- India: 'Trying To Obtain Nuclear Weapons': Israel Says 'Iran Mission' Not Complete.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: SIMMER DOWN - Tougher sanctions needed to curb parliamentary tensions, lecturer warns.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: SIMMER DOWN - Tougher sanctions needed to curb parliamentary tensions, lecturer warns.
With tensions in Jamaica’s Parliament escalating this week, a government lecturer is calling for tougher sanctions against lawmakers who breach parliamentary procedures, warning that failure to act could see the House of Representatives degenerate into a “brawl”.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: Privy Council shuts door on Dawkins Brown’s fight to regain accountant’s licence.
The United Kingdom-based Judicial Committee of the Privy Council has refused Dawkins Brown permission to appeal his removal from Jamaica’s Register of Public Accountants, bringing his latest attempt to overturn the disciplinary decision to an end. The refusal, handed down last month, means Brown has failed to secure a hearing before Jamaica’s highest appellate court in his battle against the Public Accountancy Board (PAB), which struck him off the professional register in March 2020 and ordered him to pay $1.6 million towards the costs of its disciplinary proceedings.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: Why achieving your goals can leave you feeling so empty.
THE CONVERSATION: When Anne Carson learned she had won the Nobel Prize in literature, she was in Iceland, where, according to the Swedish Academy, she was "listening to the wind". Carson didn't answer her phone right away, silencing it until her husband persuaded her to call back. Her verdict on the academy's choice: "I think you're all insane." Whatever she felt in the moment, there is an irony in Carson's Nobel win. The highest award in literature has gone to a writer who has spent her career exploring the emptiness of a desire fulfilled.
United States: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russians strike emergency workers at attack site in Komyshuvakha, Zelenskyy responds.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 13 hours ago: Russians strike emergency workers at attack site in Komyshuvakha, Zelenskyy responds.
No emergency workers were injured, but rescue equipment was damaged. Zelenskyy said search operations continue after a Russian airstrike killed 55 people.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 13 hours ago: Russia has attacked Ukraine with 115 missiles and over 3,000 drones this week, Zelenskyy reports – video.
Zelenskyy says Russia has also launched nearly 1,900 guided aerial bombs; the president has called for stronger sanctions against companies involved in missile production.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 13 hours ago: One killed and three injured in Russian attack on Dnipro suburb – photos.
A drone strike destroyed a house in a residential area. Two women and a man received medical assistance at the scene and declined hospitalisation.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 10 hours ago: People injured and houses damaged in Russian attack on Khmelnytskyi Oblast.
Firefighters extinguished a fire in Khmelnytskyi Oblast after Russian strikes damaged 12 homes and destroyed a house.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Russian strikes leave 600,000 in the dark in eastern Ukraine.
- Politico Europe, 12 hours ago: Russian strikes leave 600,000 in the dark in eastern Ukraine.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called for further sanctions on Russia ahead of talks in Abu Dhabi.

AFRICA
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Iran threatens to ‘rain down hell’ if US escalates war.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Iran threatens to ‘rain down hell’ if US escalates war.
President Trump warns that US forces are 'locked and loaded' and ready to strike, if necessary.
- Jerusalem Post, one hour ago: Trump held off on Iran strike as Israel, US prepared for military operation, sources tell 'Post'.
Israel and the US prepared for a possible strike on Iran over the weekend, but Trump held off as mediators continued efforts to reach an agreement.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: 'Iranian demands are outrageous,' Rubio says as talks fail to make progress.
Ahead of a G7 meeting in France, Rubio said Iran talks have made no progress, calling Tehran's demands "unacceptable" and warning that the US could respond to threats against its forces.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Blinken: I warned Netanyahu Israel could lose young Republicans and evangelicals.
Speaking at the Jewish Federations of North America’s General Assembly in Washington, Blinken recalled a conversation with Netanyahu in the spring of 2024 about the political consequences of the war.
Africa - bottom line: Netherlands: Sea of red fills Amsterdam streets in Gaza protest.
- Africanews, one hour ago: Netherlands: Sea of red fills Amsterdam streets in Gaza protest.
Tens of thousands of people, many dressed in red, marched through Amsterdam in the Netherlands on Sunday 8 November, demanding that the Dutch government take stronger action against Israel over the war in Gaza.
South Africa: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Aramco skyscraper damaged as Houthis target Riyadh financial district.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, NDTV - Top Stories, South China Morning Post - China, 9 hours ago: Aramco skyscraper damaged as Houthis target Riyadh financial district.
An Aramco building in Riyadh was targeted in an “attempted attack”, the Saudi energy ministry said on Sunday, with eyewitnesses telling AFP the skyscraper sustained damage, after the Saudi-led coalition fighting Houthis said it had intercepted missiles launched by the group. Houthis claimed responsibility for the attack. Aramco facilities and infrastructure have been repeatedly struck by the rebels in Yemen in recent months, with tankers, refineries, storage areas and the company headquarters all targeted by the group.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: KP plans to set up faceless ATCs, spend Rs70bn on CTD and police in a year as part of counterterrorism initiatives.
The administrative setup in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa plans to establish faceless anti-terrorism courts in the province as part of its initiatives to strengthen the fight against terrorism, according to a briefing by the officials televised on Sunday. KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi was also present at the briefing, where KP Secretary Home Amjad Ali Khan outlined several measures planned to step up the fight against terrorism and explained that witnesses in terrorism cases feared coming forward. “So, we have recently sent the amendment to set up faceless anti-terrorism courts.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 13 hours ago: Broken record: Pakistan struggles with refugee influx; US supports Iran against the Soviet Union.
As Pakistan took its first few steps, the massive logistical task of accommodating millions of refugees in the midst of widespread communal violence was a major challenge for the state. The issues of Sept 8-14, 1947, documented these difficult times. In happier news, the Urdu Anjuman met for the first time in Karachi, while in a strange twist of history, the US came to Iran’s defence in the face of Soviet threats. The great migration The partition of the subcontinent had resulted in one of the largest — and bloodiest — mass migrations in human history.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: With Stephen Miller at the helm, Trump charts a course for confrontation.
US President Donald Trump’s decision to elevate loyalist Stephen Miller to run his White House indicates that he plans to ramp up confrontation in his final two years in office and block outside political and economic pressures, Trump administration officials and other Republicans say.
India - bottom line: 'Trying To Obtain Nuclear Weapons': Israel Says 'Iran Mission' Not Complete.
- NDTV - Top Stories, The Hindu - International, 10 hours ago: 'Trying To Obtain Nuclear Weapons': Israel Says 'Iran Mission' Not Complete.
Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz renewed charges that Iran -- attacked twice since last year in major Israeli-US bombing campaigns -- is pursuing nuclear weapons, a claim that Tehran denies.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: ‘They’re a failing nation’: Trump says fresh Iran strikes ‘highly unlikely’.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 10 hours ago: Video: Jaipur cafe owner beaten after objecting to employee's friend's frequent visits.
A cafe owner named Mayank Gopalia was attacked by unidentified assailants in Jaipur on November 5. He was ambushed while walking home after closing his cafe, Oven The Bakery Cafe. The attackers repeatedly struck him with sticks, leaving him severely injured and unconscious. A preliminary investigation suggested threats from a friend of a female employee he had an altercation with earlier.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 18 hours ago: ‘Don’t talk to pups’: Drama unfolded at Faridabad police station hours before murder.
Monu Sharma allegedly shot Paramjeet Dhankar during a confrontation over a damaged gate in their parking area. Before the shooting, Sharma had threatened Dhankar at a police post, warning he would not leave him alive. The incident escalated when Sharma called Dhankar to discuss the car parking issue. Following the shooting, police teams collected evidence from the scene at the housing complex.
Asia - bottom line: India questions US ‘double standards’ as Pakistan secures F-16 upgrade deal.
- South China Morning Post - China, 15 hours ago: India questions US ‘double standards’ as Pakistan secures F-16 upgrade deal.
Washington’s decision to upgrade Pakistan’s F-16 fighter jets has drawn accusations of double standards from critics in India, who question why the United States is strengthening a nuclear-armed ally while waging war against Iran over its nuclear programme. China’s newest land-based intercontinental ballistic missile, the DF-61, has made its way into routine military training much faster than earlier ICBMs, according to state broadcaster CCTV. That raises the question of whether the People’s Liberation Army is becoming more efficient at integrating new strategic missiles into its nuclear forces. - South China Morning Post - China, one hour ago: Israel’s President Herzog gives Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form the next government.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog formally gave opposition politician Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form the next government on Sunday evening. Complex coalition negotiations still lie ahead, but it marked a significant step in the former military chief’s effort to oust Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, after elections held in a deeply divided country. - South China Morning Post - China, just now: Hong Kong records nearly 18% rise in ransomware cases amid drop in tech crime.
Hong Kong has recorded a nearly 18 per cent rise in ransomware cases in the first three quarters of this year despite an overall drop in technology crime, with police attributing the rise to artificial intelligence-aided attacks. Chief Superintendent Raymond Lam Cheuk-ho of the cybersecurity and technology crime bureau said police had recorded cases of AI agents and other forms of artificial intelligence being used in cyberattacks as recently as last month. “We understand that the use of AI...

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Poland treats fatal mass shooting as 'terrorist offence'.
- ABC News Australia, The Hindu - International, Taipei Times, just now: Poland treats fatal mass shooting as 'terrorist offence'.
Four women and two men were killed in the shooting in the Main Square of Krakow's Old Town, which Poland's defence minister has described as an "act of terror".
- ABC News Australia, 2 hours ago: Courthouse fence could leave DV survivors with no escape, lawyers warn.
Lawyers representing victims of domestic violence have warned a planned fence outside the Katherine courthouse could put their clients at risk from violent offenders.
- ABC News Australia, one hour ago: Police appeal for couple who helped friend of missing teenager.
The teenager from the Latrobe Valley likely spent the weekend wearing just shorts and boots as snow fell on nearby mountains.
- The Guardian - Australia, one hour ago: Stacey Dooley’s Australia: Off the Beaten Track review – presenting this fluffy show is beyond her.
This trip to Kangaroo Island is pleasant enough, but the investigative reporter seems lost when tackling something that doesn’t feature exploitation or outrage For years on BBC Three, Stacey Dooley equalled strife. Child labour, sexual exploitation, poverty, religious extremism, homelessness: all were ably tackled by a presenter who stood out for her lack of lofty TV-star pretension and her knack for asking the direct questions that were in audience’s minds.
